title: I Let the Axe-Throwing Lane Timer Hit the Marshal Who Wrote It

parts.text: I booked lane four at 7:18 p.m. and the laminated cap said: ONE LANE. FORTY-FIVE MINUTES. NO STAFF HOLDS. Marshal Otis palmed a second hatchet into a sleeve labeled DEMO when my group stalled on the bull. I was twenty-nine, birthday booker, holding a receipt that listed one lane. Otis shrugged. "Marshals are players of atmosphere." I photographed the sleeve, the cap, and the POS line. Then I asked for the lane log. At 7:24 the owner pinged why Otis's name was on a held-lane ticket. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see Otis's DEMO sleeve on the lane log with the cap he laminated.

social.video_title: He held a second lane under a DEMO sleeve — Part 1/2
social.description: Axe throwing, a marshal's sleeve, and a forty-five-minute cap he posted. I logged the hold. Would you have asked for the lane log?

parts.text: Otis called it flavor until the birthday group asked for the receipt. I printed the ticket, the cap, and the photo. The second hatchet went back on the wall. Otis ran the lane with one like everyone else and told the next group atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word marshals use when a POS exists. Lane policy now has a second line: MARSHALS ARE NOT PLAYERS OF THE TARGET. I keep one hatchet on a labeled hook. Otis brown-bags his jokes. The bay finally looks like a lane, not a store. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Marshals are not players of the target — Part 2/2
social.description: Lane log, owner ping, and a second line on the cap. Was DEMO ever a hold?
